// Custom Duration type with JSON marshaling support
type Duration time.Duration

func (d Duration) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error) {
    return json.Marshal(time.Duration(d).String())
}

func (d *Duration) UnmarshalJSON(data []byte) error {
    var s string
    if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &s); err == nil {
        // Try to parse as duration string (e.g., "1s", "500ms")
        if duration, err := time.ParseDuration(s); err == nil {
            *d = Duration(duration)
            return nil
        }
        
        // Try to parse as .NET TimeSpan format: [d.]HH:MM:SS[.ffffff]
        var days int
        timeStr := s
        
        // Check if it has day part (e.g., "3.12:00:30.000000")
        if dotIndex := strings.Index(s, "."); dotIndex != -1 {
            // Check if the part before first dot is a number (days)
            possibleDays := s[:dotIndex]
            if dayVal, err := strconv.Atoi(possibleDays); err == nil {
                // This looks like days, check if the rest looks like time
                remainder := s[dotIndex+1:]
                if len(remainder) >= 8 && strings.Count(remainder, ":") >= 2 {
                    days = dayVal
                    timeStr = remainder
                }
            }
        }
        
        // Parse the time part: HH:MM:SS[.ffffff]
        parts := strings.Split(timeStr, ":")
        if len(parts) == 3 {
            hours, err1 := strconv.Atoi(parts[0])
            minutes, err2 := strconv.Atoi(parts[1])
            
            if err1 == nil && err2 == nil {
                // Handle seconds with possible fractional part
                secondsPart := parts[2]
                var seconds int
                var nanoseconds int64
                
                if dotIndex := strings.Index(secondsPart, "."); dotIndex != -1 {
                    // Has fractional seconds
                    var err3 error
                    seconds, err3 = strconv.Atoi(secondsPart[:dotIndex])
                    if err3 != nil {
                        return fmt.Errorf("invalid seconds part: %s", secondsPart[:dotIndex])
                    }
                    
                    // Parse fractional part (can be up to 7 digits for .NET TimeSpan)
                    fracStr := secondsPart[dotIndex+1:]
                    // Pad or truncate to 9 digits for nanoseconds
                    if len(fracStr) > 9 {
                        fracStr = fracStr[:9]
                    } else {
                        for len(fracStr) < 9 {
                            fracStr += "0"
                        }
                    }
                    
                    frac, err4 := strconv.ParseInt(fracStr, 10, 64)
                    if err4 != nil {
                        return fmt.Errorf("invalid fractional seconds: %s", fracStr)
                    }
                    
                    nanoseconds = frac
                } else {
                    // No fractional seconds
                    var err3 error
                    seconds, err3 = strconv.Atoi(secondsPart)
                    if err3 != nil {
                        return fmt.Errorf("invalid seconds: %s", secondsPart)
                    }
                }
                
                totalDuration := time.Duration(days)*24*time.Hour + 
                               time.Duration(hours)*time.Hour + 
                               time.Duration(minutes)*time.Minute + 
                               time.Duration(seconds)*time.Second + 
                               time.Duration(nanoseconds)*time.Nanosecond
                
                *d = Duration(totalDuration)
                return nil
            }
        }
    }
    
    // Try to parse as integer (milliseconds)
    var i int64
    if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &i); err == nil {
        *d = Duration(time.Duration(i) * time.Millisecond)
        return nil
    }
    
    return fmt.Errorf("cannot unmarshal %s into Duration", string(data))
}
